newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli leader wants economic talks with Syria.
newsitem.headline: Israeli leader wants economic talks with Syria.

text.p: Israel's leader Benjamin Netanyahu said he foresaw economic talks with Syria whenever long-stalled peace moves resumed and that he had asked his finance minister to work on the issue.

"I imagine there will also be an economic track and so I have already asked Finance Minister Dan Meridor to focus on the economic issues if economic talks start with Syria," Netanyahu told Haaretz newspaper in an interview published on Wednesday.

"Syria will have much to gain on the economic side because the Syrian economy is not dashing forward. There are certain things that only with an open approach -- like joint projects -- will Syria be able to make progress," he said.

Netanyahu, elected eight months ago, said he had "various ideas" on how to advance talks with Damascus and he planned to raise them with U.S. President Bill Clinton when they meet at the White House next month. He did not elaborate.

The United States is trying to get Israel and Syria to revive peace talks launched in 1991 but suspended by Israel's previous government 10 months ago after a series of Islamist suicide bombings killed 59 people in Israel.
Netanyahu's refusal to hand back the Golan Heights -- a strategic plateau captured by Israel from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war -- has raised Syrian suspicions he is not committed to peace.
Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam has brushed aside Israeli suggestions their bilateral Middle East peace talks are about to resume.

"There is no movement until now regarding resumption of talks on the Syrian and Lebanese tracks," he said after talks with United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan in Abu Dhabi late on Tuesday.
